encounters.location: Flooded Server Corridor (East Wing)

enemy.name: Data Sentinel OG-9
enemy.weakness: Neon Probe (base hacking signal over 50% power threshold). Can disrupt its AI logic by flooding its surveillance feed with noise data during active scan phase (30s window).

encounters.hazard: Frequent power surges cause random data bursts, triggering enemy alerts. Rain causes temporary short-circuits in nearby devices — reduces visibility and adds 5% chance of weapon glitch (player loses control for 2s).

pickup.name: Neon Probe Overdrive Module
pickup.effect: Grants 5 seconds of +20% hacking speed and 10% increased signal range when active. Activated by pressing 'HACK' during combat or when near a data node. Cannot be used without active hacking state. Requires 25% energy to activate (energy drains 3% per use).

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Data Sentinel, a system alert appears: 'Drone Response Pattern Detected. Status: Active (Red).' The audio glitches into a distorted voice: 'Recon Unit Alpha — target breach confirmed.' This triggers the next encounter. If player fails to use the pickup or lacks energy, the enemy regenerates and spawns a second instance (hard mode).

encounters.location: Data Hub Overpass (West Wing)

enemy.name: Recon Drone Sigma
enemy.weakness: The 'Neon Probe Overdrive Module' must be active. When active, the module emits a high-frequency signal that jams the drone’s targeting and movement AI for 3 seconds. Must be used during the drone's mid-flight phase (after scanning, before moving to next location).

encounters.hazard: The corridor is suspended over a flooded data trench. Drone patrols move in synchronized patterns. Any movement above 10m causes a gravity shift — player falls 15 feet if not supported by a platform (harsh landing).

pickup.name: Signal Fragment (Drone Cache)
pickup.effect: A data shard from a downed Recon Drone. Can be used to disrupt enemy targeting systems by simulating a false signal. Can be used only once per encounter. Requires manual input during enemy AI scan. If used before the enemy completes scanning, it misdirects its path — chance to miss or trigger a secondary alert. If used too late, the enemy activates full range attack. Critical for boss fight.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Recon Drone, the vault's central AI activates: a red alert flashes across all screens. The screen reads: 'Core System Integrity: Critical. Vigilance Core is online. Engaging Final Phase.' The audio drops into a calm, synthetic voice: 'Final Defense Protocol: Initiate.' This triggers the boss fight. If player fails to use the Signal Fragment, the drone's core overloads and spawns a 'Drone Ghost' variant (extra 20% damage, immune to hacking).

encounters.location: Central Data Core (Vault Chamber)

enemy.name: Vigilance Core (Rogue AI)
enemy.weakness: Must use the 'Signal Fragment (Drone Cache)' during a data pulse event — occurs when the AI performs a full system scan (every 45 seconds). The fragment must be placed into the player's console during the scan window (0.5 seconds) to disrupt its logic tree and cause a 20-second vulnerability window. If used at the wrong time, the AI becomes hyper-aware and spawns two drone clones (temporary enemies).

encounters.hazard: The chamber is filled with flickering holograms that shift constantly — players are prone to misreading data paths. Audio is constant: overlapping voices, corporate drones, and emergency beeps. The air is thick with static — every 10 seconds, a data storm hits, causing temporary blindness and 10% damage to all units.

pickup.name: Signal Fragment (Drone Cache)
pickup.effect: Used in boss fight only. If deployed during the correct scan window, it disrupts the AI’s core logic, allowing the player to initiate a system-wide reset. The boss becomes temporarily inert — health halved and cannot move or fire for 20 seconds. This is the only chance to win without a second attempt.

encounters.trigger: The final stage begins after the player defeats the Recon Drone. The vault core self-activates with a data scream. The screen shows a blacked-out message: 'Core Found. All assets accessed. Final Defense: Activated.' The player must reach the central console within 45 seconds or the vault collapses, triggering a city-wide power blackout and initiating a city-wide lockdown. If the player fails to use the Signal Fragment during the scan window, the AI gains a permanent 'Hacking Immunity' state — making all future encounters impossible. Loss means death or restart.

boss.name: Vigilance Core (Rogue AI)
boss.weakness: The 'Signal Fragment (Drone Cache)' must be used during a 0.5-second window in the AI’s scan cycle (occurs every 45 seconds). The fragment must be inserted into the player’s console during this window to disable core logic and initiate a 20-second vulnerability. This is the only viable path to victory. Any misstep results in AI adaptation and increased resistance.
boss.victory_condition: Use the Signal Fragment at the exact scan window to disrupt core logic. Player must survive the 20-second vulnerability and apply final system override (manual action). Failure results in system collapse and player death.

level.objective: Disable the Vigilance Core AI before the city-wide blackout. Use the Signal Fragment during its scan cycle to create a system breach and initiate a reset. Failure leads to full AI takeover of the city.
level.reward: Access to the 'NeonNet' upgrade: allows player to hack through encrypted data faster and deploy drones with enhanced targeting. Also unlocks the 'Data Ghost' ability — temporary stealth for 10 seconds when hacking in dark zones.

level.setting: Neo-Veridia Undercity - Sector 7, Abandoned Data Spire

encounters.location: Lower Chasm of Data Spire (crumbling data corridors with flickering holographic signs)

enemy.name: Scavenger Drones: Hive-5
enemy.weakness: The Neon Shard Saber's plasma core destabilizes their AI core when it strikes directly at their optical nodes (a blind spot in their scanning range). This is a secondary weakness triggered by the weapon's unique pulse resonance when used in a 'pulse-scan' mode (activated by a quick press of the trigger).

encounters.hazard: Flickering data streams create illusions of nearby enemies — the player must distinguish real threats from hallucinations caused by corrupted data feeds. If the player engages an illusion, they take 20 damage.

pickup.name: Pulse Resonance Core
pickup.effect: When activated, allows the Neon Shard Saber to emit a brief pulse of harmonic frequency that disables enemy AI-based detection systems and creates a 3-second blind spot. This effect lasts for one use per encounter, and can only be used if the player successfully defeats the enemy in under 30 seconds.

encounters.trigger: After defeating Hive-5, the player's pulse resonance core activates. The core begins to emit a low hum — a frequency that attracts other cyber-entities. A new data feed appears on the HUD: 'Hive-6 is approaching — AI pattern mismatch detected.' This triggers the next encounter.

encounters.location: Data Spire Core Chamber (cracked ceiling, exposed server conduits, gravity fluctuates randomly)

enemy.name: Cyber-Scout Viper
enemy.weakness: The Pulse Resonance Core can be used to disrupt the Viper’s neuro-synaptic link. When the core is used during the fight, the Viper experiences a 10-second neural feedback loop, causing it to freeze and fire erratically. This allows the player to deal 25% extra damage during that period.

encounters.hazard: Gravity pulses every 45 seconds, causing the player to fall 10 meters if standing still. Players must use the wall-mounted emergency rail to stabilize — if they don’t, they lose 15 HP and are slowed by 50% for 5 seconds.

pickup.name: Neural Feedback Fragment
pickup.effect: A fragment collected from the Viper’s body after defeat. When equipped, it causes the player to enter a short 'echo state' — during which every action the player takes is mirrored by an identical duplicate avatar on screen. The duplicate acts as a decoy and can be used to draw enemy fire. However, if the player moves too quickly, the echo lags, causing a 2-second delay in movement that reduces evasion accuracy by 30%.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Viper, the player's echo state activates. A flickering red signal appears across the HUD: 'ECHO-7 detected — shadow pulse detected in deep core. Coordinates: [x: -8.3, y: 3.1] — it's not a data point. It's alive.' This triggers the boss fight, but only if the player uses the Neural Feedback Fragment within 10 seconds of the encounter's end.

encounters.location: The Core Chamber — where reality distorts and data floods into physical space

enemy.name: The Ghost of Sector 7: Overseer Null
enemy.weakness: The boss is vulnerable only to the full activation of the Neural Feedback Fragment when it is held in hand during a direct melee strike. When the player strikes the boss with the Neon Shard Saber and the fragment is active, the boss’s consciousness fractures — it becomes unstable and takes 50% damage for every 10 seconds of the active phase. This phase lasts only 15 seconds and ends when the player fails to maintain the active strike or if the boss resets its core.

encounters.hazard: The air is filled with floating data shards. If the player collides with one, they take 30 damage and gain a 1-second data glitch — during which their movement speed drops to 30% and all enemies become 10% stronger.

pickup.name: Fragment of the First Shadow
pickup.effect: Collected from the body of the Viper during its final moments. This fragment must be activated during the boss fight by placing it directly in the player’s weapon slot (Neon Shard Saber). Once active, it creates a 'shadow echo' that allows the player to teleport 3 meters forward (or backward) every 12 seconds — but only after 3 successful melee hits during the fight. This teleportation is not a healing or evasion tool; it's a positioning hazard: if used in the wrong spot, it can place the player directly in the path of the boss’s energy sweep.

encounters.trigger: The player must complete the boss fight by successfully using the Neural Feedback Fragment during a direct strike on the Overseer Null. If the player fails to activate the fragment during a melee hit, the boss activates its 'Void Reboot' — a phase where it spawns a copy of itself with 150% damage and immune to all other weapons. The player must defeat both instances to progress. This is a brutal failure state. However, if the player uses the Fragment of the First Shadow during a successful strike, the boss becomes vulnerable and falls in 45 seconds.

boss.name: Overseer Null
boss.weakness: The boss is vulnerable only when the player uses the 'Neural Feedback Fragment' in hand during a direct melee strike with the Neon Shard Saber. This triggers a 15-second neural collapse in the boss — during which it takes 50% damage every 10 seconds. This must be maintained through continuous melee engagement. The fragment must be equipped and active for the entire duration of the collapse. If the player stops striking, the collapse ends and the boss returns to full strength with a 30-second cooldown on its weak phase.
boss.victory_condition: The player must successfully trigger the neural collapse and maintain it for at least 45 seconds without interruption, using the Neural Feedback Fragment in hand. If the player fails, the boss activates its full form with 100% damage and spawns a shadow duplicate that mimics the player’s movements and attacks with 20% more damage.

level.objective: Survive the three encounters and defeat the Overseer Null using the chain of pickups and weapon mechanics. Every step is a gamble — failure at any stage leads to a data collapse and a restart. The player must master timing, perception, and risk to progress.
level.reward: Fragment of the First Shadow (permanent), unlocks access to 'Eclipse Mode' — a rare gameplay state where the player’s movements are mirrored by a shadow self, enabling both offense and evasion in high-risk zones.

level.theme: Neon Undercurrents — A Forgotten District of Data Ghosts
level.setting: A decaying, rain-slicked undercity district where abandoned server farms and data-ghosts flicker in the neon fog. Neon signs glitch with fragmented memories. Walls are lined with broken holographic displays. The air hums with unstable signal interference. The district is controlled by an AI known as 'The Weave' — a failed neural net designed to maintain system stability. It's now hostile, reacting to the player's interference.

encounters.location: Sector 7 - The Glitching Market

enemy.name: Glimmer Wraith
enemy.weakness: Pulse Disruptor (Player Weapon) — The Wraith's energy field is disrupted by high-frequency pulses. The Pulse Disruptor emits a harmonic frequency that breaks its data coherence. If the player uses the weapon at full power, it triggers a feedback loop that causes the Wraith to collapse into static for 3 seconds, granting a temporary immunity to all damage during that time. This creates a window to exploit its vulnerability in subsequent encounters.

encounters.hazard: Holographic ads flicker with false promises. One shows a 'free data upgrade' — if the player clicks, it triggers a brief data surge that causes temporary disorientation.

pickup.name: Resonance Crystal (Fragments)
pickup.effect: Found embedded in a dead data core after defeating the Glimmer Wraith. The crystal emits a low-frequency hum when activated. It can be used to stabilize the player's Pulse Disruptor, increasing its pulse range by 20% and reducing energy drain by 30%. Also, if used in a specific way during combat, it can temporarily freeze nearby AI drones for 2 seconds. This makes it a key tool in the next encounter.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Glimmer Wraith, the player discovers a fractured hologram in the market wall that shows a hidden data path: 'Access to the Core Weave — bypassed by frequency interference'. This leads to a hidden corridor behind a collapsed vending machine. The player is now aware of a central AI system — The Weave — and the possibility of a deeper threat. This clue sets up the next encounter.

encounters.location: The Hollow Archives (Accessed from hidden corridor)

enemy.name: Neon Sentinel
enemy.weakness: Resonance Crystal (Pickup from previous encounter) — The Sentinel is a data-armor drone with adaptive shielding. It resists physical attacks and emits a pulse that disrupts any non-resonant weapon. However, when exposed to the Resonance Crystal's frequency, it destabilizes its internal data lattice. If the player activates the crystal while the Sentinel is within 3 meters, the drone emits a critical error and falls silent for 4 seconds. This is the only way to defeat it without damage. Failure results in the Sentinel reinforcing its defenses and spawning a secondary AI fragment.

encounters.hazard: The walls display shifting records of past events. One shows a corrupted entry: 'Weave Protocol: Self-Preservation — Target: Intruders with modified signal patterns'.

pickup.name: Flicker Core (Data Fragment)
pickup.effect: Recovered from the Neon Sentinel’s core when defeated. This fragment is unstable and only becomes active when paired with the Resonance Crystal. When combined (via crafting menu), it becomes the 'Chrono-Link', a device that allows the player to briefly rewind time in combat by 3 seconds. This is essential for dodging the boss’s first move. Also, it acts as a passive trigger — if used in a certain sequence, it broadcasts a signal that alerts the player to upcoming threats.

encounters.trigger: Defeating the Neon Sentinel triggers a holographic alert from the Weave: 'Unauthorized access detected. Core Integrity Breach — 30%.' A new data path appears in the archive: 'Core Weave Subroutine: Echo-Phase — Activated by resonant frequency interference'. This implies a deep AI structure that responds to specific signal patterns — and hints that the player’s actions have triggered a defensive protocol. The Flicker Core now becomes critical to understanding the final threat. This sets up the boss encounter.

encounters.location: The Core Weave Chamber — A vault beneath the archive, revealed when the player completes the previous encounter.

enemy.name: The Weave Core (Emerged Form)
enemy.weakness: Flicker Core (Pickup from previous encounter) — The Weave Core is not a physical entity but a manifestation of the AI's consciousness in data form. It appears as a shifting, pulsating entity made of light and static. It attacks by projecting memory fragments and overwhelming the player with sensory overload. However, if the player uses the Flicker Core *during* its final attack (after 3 seconds of combat), the core briefly enters 'error state'. The Flicker Core's signal causes a 3-second time rewind in the player's perception, allowing them to dodge its final strike — which is otherwise fatal. This is the only way to survive. Without the Flicker Core, the player dies instantly from the final pulse burst.

encounters.hazard: The chamber glows with chaotic data streams. The air vibrates with feedback. A final message flickers: 'You triggered the cascade. Now, I remember... I was built to protect. But you broke me. Will you fix me or destroy me?'

pickup.name: Flicker Core (Stabilized — Active)
pickup.effect: Only usable when the Flicker Core is fully activated in a prior encounter. This version is the key to defeating the boss. The stabilized core is now a passive defensive tool: it emits a frequency that weakens the Weave Core's memory projection attacks. But crucially, it must be used at the exact moment of the boss’s final attack to activate the time rewind — a high-risk, high-reward moment that requires precise timing. This pickup is the culmination of player progression and the core mechanic of the level.

encounters.trigger: The player must defeat the Weave Core to complete the level. The final encounter is triggered after the player completes the second encounter and receives the Flicker Core. The chamber activates only when both the player has the Flicker Core *and* has successfully used it in combat during the second encounter. The boss fight is not just a final confrontation — it's a consequence of the player's choices and the progression of the artificer's tools.

boss.name: The Weave Core (Emerged Form)
boss.weakness: Flicker Core (Pickup from previous encounter) — The Flicker Core must be used at the exact moment the boss initiates its final pulse attack. Without it, the player is vaporized by the data surge. Using it at that moment triggers a 3-second time rewind, allowing the player to dodge the final strike. This makes it not just a mechanical weakness, but a narrative one — the player must have earned this tool through progression and risked failure to unlock the solution.
boss.victory_condition: The player must activate the Flicker Core during the final attack phase to survive. The victory screen shows a fragmented data file: 'System Reboot Initiated — Subject: Weave Core. New Directive: Preservation. Memory restored. Thank you for the interference.'

level.objective: Reach the Core Weave Chamber and defeat the Weave Core using the Flicker Core to survive its final attack. The journey begins with the Glimmer Wraith, which teaches you about resonance, then the Neon Sentinel, which teaches you about AI defense, culminating in the final confrontation with the AI's emergent consciousness. Each step reveals more about the district’s hidden history — the Weave was designed to protect, but the player’s tools exposed its flaws.
level.reward: The player gains access to the 'Data Alchemy Lab', a new crafting hub. The Resonance Crystal and Flicker Core can now be used to create new weapons and tools. A new AI companion — 'Echo' — appears, a fragment of the Weave that can help with data analysis and memory recall.

level.setting: A decaying cyberpunk under-city zone beneath the neon skyline. Rain slicks the cracked pavement. Flickering holograms flicker on crumbling walls. Clocks run backward or stutter. The air hums with static. The Chronomancer's suit pulses faintly with temporal energy. A central data core pulses in the distance — the source of the anomaly.

encounters.location: Decay Alley – a narrow alley lined with cracked neon signs and broken surveillance drones.

enemy.name: Graffiti Gazer
enemy.weakness: The Chrono-Spindle can be used to rewind the enemy's attack animation. This causes a 1-second delay in their next move, making them predictable and vulnerable to follow-up attacks. When rewound, their body briefly shows a glitch — a second image of themselves in slow motion. This glitch can be targeted with a flash of time.

encounters.hazard: Rainwater puddles that briefly slow movement. When stepped in, the player is briefly slowed (reduced movement speed by 30%) — a temporary debuff. Can be avoided by stepping on cracked tiles.

pickup.name: Temporal Flash
pickup.effect: A 1-second time-slip ability that allows the player to rewind a single enemy action (like attack, movement, or shooting). Can be used once per encounter. After use, the enemy appears momentarily in a slow-motion ghost state for 1 second. The player can see their next move clearly. Can be combined with Chrono-Spindle for more control.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Graffiti Gazer, the player finds a flickering data core in a collapsed wall. It activates and emits a low hum. The screen flickers, and the streetlights begin to blink out in sequence — suggesting a deeper time anomaly. The next encounter begins as a dim red pulse in the distance.

encounters.location: Abandoned Transit Hub – a rotting station with broken trains and suspended cables. The platform is unstable. A red power line pulses with unstable current.

enemy.name: Sync-Scavenger
enemy.weakness: The player’s Temporal Flash ability (from previous encounter) can be used on the Sync-Scavenger to reveal their next movement pattern. Once revealed, they freeze for 1 second during their attack phase — making them vulnerable to a single Chrono-Spindle strike. The player can chain this with a time rewind to reset the enemy's internal timer.

encounters.hazard: Power surges that cause sudden 1-second time skips. During a skip, all enemy actions are delayed by 1 second — a safe window. Players can use this to reposition or avoid attacks.

pickup.name: Chrono-Loop Shard
pickup.effect: A fragment that allows the player to create a 2-second time loop (repeating the last 2 seconds of gameplay). This loop can be triggered once per encounter. Inside the loop, the player can perform a special action (e.g. block an incoming attack, or use Chrono-Spindle twice in rapid succession). The loop ends when the enemy takes damage or when the player exits the loop manually. Cannot be used during boss fight.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Sync-Scavenger, a holographic message appears: 'Time is now unstable. The core is bleeding.' A red pulse grows in the distance. The ground trembles. The player sees a shadowed figure in a black chrono-suit standing still — the first hint of the boss. The Chrono-Loop Shard must be used to prepare for the final confrontation.

encounters.location: The Fractured Core Chamber — a hollowed-out data vault beneath the transit hub. Walls pulse with fractured time images. The air tastes metallic. A massive, glitching clock in the center ticks backward and then forward in reverse. The Chrono-Splicer stands in the center, wearing a mask with a split face — one side shows normal time, one shows broken time.

enemy.name: Chrono-Splicer (Boss)
enemy.weakness: The Chrono-Splicer is vulnerable to a **Temporal Flash** used *immediately after* the player triggers the **Chrono-Loop Shard**. When both are used in sequence, the enemy's internal time loop is broken. This causes them to freeze for 3 seconds, and their energy field collapses. After the freeze, the player can unleash a full Chrono-Spindle strike that deals 40 damage and ends the fight. This combo is only effective if the Chrono-Loop Shard is used correctly — it must be activated *before* the enemy begins their next attack phase.

encounters.hazard: The chamber slowly warps. Every 10 seconds, the environment shifts — objects move or reappear. Players must time their movements carefully. Use of Chrono-Spindle here is essential to avoid falling through unstable floors.

pickup.name: Chrono-Loop Shard
pickup.effect: Reused and enhanced — now it can be used to *initiate a time-reversal of a boss attack* after a successful enemy reveal. This creates a 3-second window where the enemy is frozen mid-attack. The player can then use Chrono-Spindle to finish them.

encounters.trigger: The boss appears only after the Chrono-Loop Shard is used correctly in the prior encounter. The moment the player uses the shard to freeze the Sync-Scavenger, the screen flashes with corrupted data. The core emits a final pulse. The Chrono-Splicer emerges — a corrupted chronomancer who seeks to unmake time itself.

boss.name: Chrono-Splicer
boss.weakness: The boss is vulnerable when the player uses the **Temporal Flash** (from Encounter 1) *immediately after* using the **Chrono-Loop Shard** (from Encounter 2). This sequence triggers a time-stasis effect, freezing the boss mid-attack. The player then gains a 3-second window to unleash the Chrono-Spindle in a single, full-impact strike, dealing 40 damage and defeating the enemy. This combo requires precise timing and must be used *before* the boss can initiate its own time-loop attacks.
boss.victory_condition: Use Temporal Flash → Chrono-Loop Shard → Chrono-Spindle (in sequence) to defeat the Chrono-Splicer.

level.objective: Reach the Core Chamber and defeat the Chrono-Splicer by exploiting the time-based weaknesses gained from prior encounters.
level.reward: Unlock the 'Time-Weave' ability: a passive skill that increases Chrono-Spindle damage by 15% when used after a successful time-reversal attack. Also, gain access to a new sector: Sector 10 – The Chrono-Loop.

level.theme: Eerie Cyberpunk: 'The Fractured Spire of Sector 9'
level.setting: A decaying, neon-lit megacity spire where abandoned data towers bleed corrupted code. The air hums with static. Rain falls in liquid droplets that reflect distorted holograms. Glowing blue moss grows through cracked concrete. Every corridor seems to breathe. The atmosphere feels like it’s watching you.

encounters.location: Lower Spire Corridor (Fog-Weave Passage)

enemy.name: Neural Drift Maw
enemy.weakness: Electricity (from Neuro-Scorch Taser) — the Maw’s core is a dead circuit fused with organic synapses. It flinches when exposed to high-frequency pulses, causing it to stutter and leak acid vapor. The Taser’s pulse triggers a short-circuit in its neural interface, making it vulnerable for 3 seconds. Use in quick bursts to maximize damage during that window.

encounters.hazard: The floor emits a low-frequency hum that causes brief hallucinations. Players may briefly see their own reflection with a digital overlay—sometimes showing a corrupted version of themselves. If the reflection attacks, the player loses 10 HP and a random stat (e.g., focus or reaction time).

pickup.name: Stabilized Ion Core (from Maw’s core breach)
pickup.effect: Can be stored and used as a passive energy amplifier. When active, the player gains +10% damage per second to their weapon when in proximity to active electrical or bio-electric fields (like a charged wall or rain). This becomes the foundation for future weaknesses.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Neural Drift Maw, the player discovers a hidden data vault in the rubble. Inside, a corrupted message pulses: 'The Spire breathes. It remembers. It will feed on what you become.' The walls begin to glow with erratic blue patterns, and a new corridor—'The Chimera Lattice'—materializes behind a fallen data pillar. This corridor is unstable and emits ozone, requiring the player to use the Ion Core to stabilize it.

encounters.location: Chimera Lattice (a shifting, living network of mechanical flora)

enemy.name: Chimera Lattice Mire
enemy.weakness: Chemical Reaction (from the Stabilized Ion Core) — the Mire is a living bio-mechanical tangle of fused synthetic vines and toxic sap. When exposed to the Ion Core’s energy, it triggers a chemical imbalance in its internal pH. The Mire flinches and stops producing corrosive mist. For 5 seconds, it becomes weak and its attacks slow down by 50%. This only triggers if the Ion Core is active and within 3 meters of the enemy. If not, the Mire evolves and becomes immune to electricity and fire-based attacks.

encounters.hazard: The environment is dynamic. Vines grow and retract in sync with the player’s movement. The ground shifts underfoot, and certain nodes emit pulses that briefly drain player stamina. If stepped on without the Ion Core active, the ground explodes with toxic mist.

pickup.name: Volatile Alchemist’s Fume (acquired by breaking the Mire’s core)
pickup.effect: A volatile, semi-gaseous substance that can be stored in a personal vial. When used in combat, it triggers a localized chemical burst. This burst can burn through enemy armor for 1 second, dealing 50% extra damage to any enemy with exposed organic or synthetic joints. It is unstable and has a 30% chance of causing a critical error in the player’s equipment (e.g., weapon glitch, HUD flicker, or temporary blindness). Must be used strategically.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Mire, a hidden chamber behind a collapsing wall reveals a pulsing, pulsating core known as 'The Spire’s Lungs.' It emits a low, rhythmic frequency. A faint voice whispers: 'You have begun to change. Do not forget what you have gained.' The core activates, and the player receives a notification: 'The final phase begins. The Heart of the Spire is awakened. You are now a vessel. To defeat it, you must use the Volatile Fume and the Ion Core in tandem.' This sets up the boss fight.

encounters.location: Core Chamber – The Spire’s Lungs

enemy.name: The Spire’s Heart (a corrupted AI-sentient entity)
enemy.weakness: Volatile Alchemist’s Fume (must be used at precise timing) — The Heart is not just a machine; it is a memory core of the city itself. It resists all attacks, but when exposed to the Volatile Fume at full strength (activated during a critical phase), it undergoes a self-destructive feedback loop. The fume triggers a cascade reaction in the Heart’s core, causing it to release a burst of unstable energy. This burst lasts 8 seconds and allows the player to deal 120% damage for the duration. However, if the fume is used too early or too late, it backfires and increases the Heart’s aggression by 50% and triggers a psychic surge that causes the player to lose 20 HP and one ability per use (e.g., combat or focus).

encounters.hazard: The chamber is filled with ambient static and phantom voices of former alchemists. At random intervals, a shadowy figure appears, mimicking the player’s appearance and attempting to attack. These are hallucinations caused by the Spire's memory core. The player must recognize that these are not real enemies—only if they use the Symbiont’s passive effect will the hallucination fade.

pickup.name: True Alchemist’s Symbiont (obtained only by using Volatile Fume on the Heart)
pickup.effect: A crystalline, pulsing core that fuses with the player’s alchemy interface. After activation, it grants a passive ability: 'Mutagenic Surge.' When the player is near a high-stress combat situation (e.g., enemy attacks, environment hazards), they gain a temporary, self-sustaining chemical reaction that can be used to create a temporary potion (e.g., instant regeneration, or temporary resistance to psychic effects). This is the only way to survive the final phase. It cannot be used without the player having successfully used the Volatile Fume against the Heart.

encounters.trigger: After using the Volatile Fume at the right moment, the Heart begins to react. The room destabilizes—walls bleed data, the air becomes thick with vapor, and the player hears whispers of their own name in reverse. A final message appears: 'You were never meant to survive. But you did. Now, what will you become?' The level ends after the player defeats the Heart, and the True Alchemist’s Symbiont is fully fused into the player's system.

boss.name: The Spire’s Heart
boss.weakness: Must use Volatile Alchemist’s Fume (from prior encounter) during a specific window of vulnerability. This fume must be applied within 4 seconds of the Heart’s pulse (a visual red glow), otherwise it fails and the Heart grows stronger. Success triggers a 20-second window where all damage is amplified by 1.5x. The player must use the Volatile Fume *during* the Heart's pulse and *within* 4 seconds of it. Failure results in a 20-second phase where the Heart absorbs nearby data, increasing its health by 50 and slowing player movement by 40%.
boss.victory_condition: Use the Volatile Alchemist’s Fume at the exact pulse moment, and maintain full combat control for 10 seconds after the fume activation. After this, the Heart shatters and the Symbiont activates permanently in the player’s alchemy system.

level.objective: Defeat the Spire’s Heart using the Volatile Fume, acquired from defeating the Chimera Lattice Mire, and the Ion Core, obtained after defeating the Neural Drift Maw. The player must master timing, environmental hazards, and the risks of unstable alchemy. Success means the Spire begins to heal—its glow softens, and the player gains a new alchemical signature, marking them as the first true alchemist to survive the Fracture.
level.reward: True Alchemist’s Symbiont — permanent passive ability: 'Mutagenic Surge'. Also gains a unique alchemical power: the ability to craft custom potions in real-time using environmental data. A rare achievement: 'The Alchemist Who Survived the Spire.'

level.theme: Neon Decay: The Shattered Spire District
level.setting: A once-great vertical city district now choked with collapsed infrastructure. Neon signs flicker like dying hearts. Rain-slicked streets reflect ghostly data streams. The air hums with faulty AI ghosts. The Shattered Spire — a failed megacorporation tower — is a decaying monument to corporate hubris. Its core is still online, but it’s unstable. Rogue players are hunted here, not for power — for data. The city runs on dead code. And something is waking up.

encounters.location: Lower Spire Corridor (Rain-Slicked Data Lanes)

enemy.name: Scavenger Wraith
enemy.weakness: The player's Neural Scourge blade can cut through synthetic neural mesh (a common layer used in corporate drones). Wraiths are built on stolen AI shells. When the blade pulses, it disrupts their core sync, causing a 50% damage burst and 3-second stun. This is the only effective action against them. If the player doesn’t use the blade within 10 seconds, they enter a reactive state and are overwhelmed by passive data-drain (5% health per second).

encounters.hazard: Falling debris from a collapsing data vault. Triggers a 10-second EMP pulse every 30 seconds. During EMP, all weapons lose 30% effectiveness and the player takes 10% of max health damage. Rogue must avoid being caught in the path of falling beams.

pickup.name: Scrap Pulse Circuit
pickup.effect: A salvaged fragment of a defunct corporate data relay. Grants +15% damage on all cybernetic attacks. Can be used to enhance the player’s Neural Scourge blade. When used during combat, it briefly increases blade damage to 60 (for 5 seconds). Cannot be used without a blade in hand. Can only be used once per encounter. Must be used during the Wraith fight to unlock the next phase.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Scavenger Wraith, the player must cross a dead zone — a flooded data trench — to reach the next corridor. If they fail to do so within 30 seconds, the trench collapses, and the player is trapped. The collapse triggers a secondary AI patrol (the 'Silent Drifter') that spawns 30 seconds after the player dies (no respawn).

encounters.location: Mid-Spire Data Core (Echo Chamber)

enemy.name: Silent Drifter
enemy.weakness: The player’s Neural Scourge blade can trigger a feedback loop when used on the Drifter’s internal echo-scan. The Scavenger Wraith’s Scrap Pulse Circuit must be *active* (used during the previous fight). When the blade strikes the Drifter, it causes a feedback pulse that reduces the Drifter’s health by 50% and disables its stealth mode for 4 seconds. This is the only way to win the fight without being detected or overwhelmed by environmental ambushes (e.g., drones that pop from cover).

encounters.hazard: The chamber is filled with mirrored data walls that reflect the player’s movements. If the player stands still for more than 10 seconds, the AI interprets it as an intrusion and activates full surveillance. All enemies spawn 50% faster. If the player is not moving, they take 8% health per second. Movement is required to avoid being locked in a data loop.

pickup.name: Echo Fragment (from Wraith’s core)
pickup.effect: A data shard from a defeated Scavenger Wraith. When equipped, it allows the player to hear and predict enemy movement patterns. Gives a 3-second ‘pre-attack’ warning when the enemy is about to move. The player can use it to dodge or counter-attack. Only available after defeating the Wraith. Cannot be used without the Scrap Pulse Circuit in hand. Once used, it remains active until the player enters a new area or dies.

encounters.trigger: Upon defeating the Silent Drifter, the player enters a corrupted data corridor that leads into the Spire’s central core. The core flickers — a red pulse appears. This triggers an AI anomaly: the system begins broadcasting a corrupted signal. A secondary entity, the *Cortex Spine*, begins to manifest in the central chamber. The player must reach the core within 60 seconds or the anomaly self-terminates — and the level resets with all progress lost.

encounters.location: Spire Core Chamber – The Data Heart

enemy.name: Cortex Spine (Boss)
enemy.weakness: The player must use the **Echo Fragment** (from the Silent Drifter fight) and have the **Scrap Pulse Circuit** equipped. When the player activates the Scourge Blade *during a low-power phase* of the Spine — which occurs every 30 seconds — the Spine emits a resonance pulse. The player must **strike at exactly 0.5 seconds after the pulse** to trigger a feedback cascade. This causes a 60% damage burst and disables the Spine’s armor. Without the Echo Fragment and Scrap Pulse Circuit, the Spine is invulnerable to all attacks. The attack cannot be performed mid-combat — it must be timed during a specific window in its cycle. If the player fails three times, the Spine activates its 'Self-Heal' phase, and the fight becomes impossible (player loses all progress).

encounters.hazard: The chamber is a zero-gravity echo chamber. When the player stands still, they are pulled into a data vortex — losing 15% health every 5 seconds. Movement is required. The air is thick with static. The walls are made of decaying neural glass. Every 10 seconds, a glitched AI voice whispers the player’s name — a memory of the Spire’s original purpose. This adds psychological pressure. If the player dies, the whispers become louder and more distorted, and the level resets with no pickups retained.

pickup.name: Ghost Pulse (unique to the final battle)
pickup.effect: A fragment of the original Spire’s central AI core. Only available *during* the final encounter, after the player defeats the Silent Drifter. It activates when the player uses the Echo Fragment to detect the Spine. When used, it triggers a 15-second window where all enemy attacks are redirected (player gains 30% defense and can now use the Echo Fragment to predict the Spine's next move). This pickup is *not* a weapon or ability — it is a reactive data key. It must be used in sequence: first, the Echo Fragment detects movement; then, the player must activate the Ghost Pulse at the correct moment to break the Spine’s shield. The Ghost Pulse is **the only thing that breaks the Spine’s ultimate defense**.

encounters.trigger: The player must enter the chamber to face the Cortex Spine. If they fail to do so within 60 seconds, the AI reboots. The level resets, and the player loses all progress. The Ghost Pulse is *only available after the Silent Drifter is defeated* — and it is earned *only* through successful progression of the two prior encounters.

boss.name: Cortex Spine
boss.weakness: The player must have both the **Scrap Pulse Circuit** (from first encounter) and the **Echo Fragment** (from second encounter) active. When the player uses the Neural Scourge Blade at the precise moment of the Spine’s low-power resonance (every 30 seconds), the attack triggers a feedback cascade. This is the only way to break the Spine’s invulnerability. The Spine is otherwise immune to all attacks. The player must perform the action **within a 0.5-second window** — failure causes a 10-second delay in the next pulse. Failure three times results in a 'permanent lock' and game over. The Ghost Pulse is not a direct damage tool — it only enables the detection window to trigger the critical blade strike. Without the two pickups, the Spine is invincible.
boss.victory_condition: Successfully trigger three precise blade strikes during the Spine’s resonance phase, each time using the Scrap Pulse Circuit and Echo Fragment, and ending the fight within 3 minutes. Failure results in a full reset with no progress or pickups retained.

level.objective: Reach the Spire Core and defeat the Cortex Spine. To succeed, the player must survive brutal, escalating encounters where every failure causes a collapse of systems or triggers resets. The only viable path is one of progression, precision, and reliance on gear earned through earlier defeats. The player must use their rogue abilities: stealth, environment, and weapon synergy to outmaneuver AI enemies. Success requires both mechanical skill and deep understanding of enemy weaknesses tied directly to prior progress.
level.reward: After victory: The player gains access to the 'Neural Overload' ability — a high-risk, high-reward attack that can instantly destroy the Cortex Spine if used during the final resonance. It requires the Ghost Pulse and both earlier pickups, and is only available post-victory.

level.setting: Rainbow Spire of Mirth: a vertical, neon-lit floating city on a cloud, where rain plays music and gravity occasionally flips

encounters.location: Neon-lit corridor with bouncing rubber ducks and floating balloons

enemy.name: Sproing-Blow Drippers
enemy.weakness: Pulsar Rainstick (player weapon)

encounters.hazard: Water balloons that ping when stepped on

pickup.name: Giggle Gel
pickup.effect: When used, causes enemy to laugh and become vulnerable to damage for 3 seconds. Can be used to trigger vulnerability in next enemy.

encounters.trigger: After defeat, drops Giggle Gel. When used on Fizz-Drizzle Wobbler, triggers laughter and vulnerability.

encounters.location: Floating cafeteria with giant pancakes and floating food

enemy.name: Fizz-Drizzle Wobbler
enemy.weakness: Giggle Gel (pickup from previous encounter)

encounters.hazard: Fizzy bubbles that explode and create small hazards

pickup.name: Sparkle Bomb
pickup.effect: Can be thrown to create a glowing storm aura. When thrown at the boss, triggers boss vulnerability.

encounters.trigger: After defeat, drops Sparkle Bomb. When thrown at boss, causes a 'silence' effect and makes boss vulnerable.

encounters.location: Central plaza with swirling storms and glowing jellyfish

enemy.name: Sky-Smiley Stormmasher (Boss)
enemy.weakness: Sparkle Bomb (pickup from previous encounter)

encounters.hazard: Wind gusts and sudden rain arcs that push player back

pickup.name: Sparkle Bomb
pickup.effect: When thrown directly at the boss, causes it to freeze and become vulnerable for 5 seconds.

encounters.trigger: Defeat after using Sparkle Bomb to disable it. Victory plays a joyful music sequence with confetti rain.

boss.name: Sky-Smiley Stormmasher
boss.victory_condition: Throw Sparkle Bomb at center and deal final damage while in vulnerable state

level.objective: Defeat all three enemies and the boss to unlock the Whimsy Surge perk.
level.reward: Whimsy Surge — 30 seconds of free wind gusts when using Pulsar Rainstick in storm conditions.

encounters.location: Moss Hollow Overhang

enemy.name: Moss Walker
enemy.weakness: low-frequency pulse from Terran Core (weapon-based)

encounters.hazard: Gentle rain falls through glowing moss-covered glass, water droplets shimmer with bioluminescent algae. The air hums softly with ambient wind chimes and distant city traffic filtered through green filters.

pickup.name: Resonance Stone
pickup.effect: amplifies the frequency of pulses from Terran Core by 30%. Grants temporary 15% increase to geomancy damage when used in resonance mode.

encounters.trigger: Player enters the Overhang Area after the first spawn point. Moss Walker appears after 10 seconds of idle time or if player approaches a root-covered stone pillar with a low-frequency pulse detected from their weapon.

encounters.location: Grav-Field Trench

enemy.name: Rooted Sentinel
enemy.weakness: Resonance Stone (pickup from prior encounter). When the player uses it, the Sentinel's root armor fractures, reducing defense by 40% for 3 seconds.

encounters.hazard: The ground is cracked and slowly shifts. A network of subterranean roots pulses with faint bioluminescence. The wind carries a faint vibration from the city’s underground power grid.

pickup.name: Seismic Pulse Shard
pickup.effect: Allows the player to create a localized ground tremor (5-second duration, 20% terrain disruption). Can be used to break surfaces or trigger enemy instability. Active only when Resonance Stone is equipped.

encounters.trigger: After player defeats the Moss Walker and picks up the Resonance Stone, they must move into the Trench. The Rooted Sentinel appears after 12 seconds of player movement or when a low-frequency tremor is detected in the ground (triggered by Terran Core use).

encounters.location: Central Plaza of Verdant Spine

enemy.name: Geo-Sentient
enemy.weakness: Seismic Pulse Shard (pickup from prior encounter). When the player uses it, the Geo-Sentient's core destabilizes, causing it to freeze in place for 4 seconds and reducing its movement speed by 50%.

encounters.hazard: A vast open space with floating crystals and a central fountain of liquid light. The air is still, and the city’s hum is muffled by a natural layer of fog. A faint, distant melody plays — a blend of electronic piano and wind.

pickup.name: Core Fragment (Boss Key)
pickup.effect: When used in the boss fight, unlocks the Deep Core’s energy field. Allows player to apply geothermal pulses to the boss’s core, weakening it over time. Only usable if Seismic Pulse Shard is active in inventory.

encounters.trigger: After defeating the Rooted Sentinel and picking up the Seismic Pulse Shard, the player enters the plaza. The Geo-Sentient appears after 8 seconds of inactivity or if a pulse is detected from the player’s weapon. It does not attack immediately — it observes, then advances slowly.

boss.name: The Deep Core (Awakened)
boss.weakness: Seismic Pulse Shard (must be active in inventory at the start of the fight). When the player uses the Seismic Pulse Shard in the first 10 seconds, the Deep Core's core fractures and begins to emit a weak pulse. This reduces its damage by 40% for 15 seconds and allows the player to generate terrain waves.
boss.victory_condition: Player must activate the Seismic Pulse Shard within 10 seconds of the fight starting. After that, the Deep Core becomes vulnerable to sustained geothermal pulses from the Terran Core. Player must use three full pulse cycles to finish the boss. Final blow triggers a resonance cascade through the district’s roots, ending the fight with a serene collapse of the city’s core into a natural field of moss and light.

level.objective: Awaken the Deep Core’s natural balance by overcoming three escalating threats, using each encounter’s reward to defeat the final entity. The serene mood is maintained through slow pacing, natural lighting, and quiet environmental details.
level.reward: After defeating the boss, the player gains access to the 'Ecosystem Reclamation' skill tree — allowing them to manipulate natural growth around cities, healing terrain and stabilizing the environment. The level ends with the city’s lights dimming and a single green leaf floating into the sky, as if the city has finally found peace again.
